interface.signature: def getHappyString(n: int, k: int) -> str:

preconditions.description: n and k are within the specified constraints (1 ≤ n ≤ 10, 1 ≤ k ≤ 100).

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == n and all(c in ['a', 'b', 'c'] for c in return_value) and all(return_value[i] != return_value[i + 1] for i in range(n - 1))
postconditions.description: The returned string is a happy string of length n, meaning it consists only of 'a', 'b', or 'c', and no two adjacent characters are the same.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '' or (all(return_value != happy_strings[n][i] for i in range(k - 1)) and return_value == happy_strings[n][k - 1])
postconditions.description: If k exceeds the number of happy strings of length n, return an empty string. Otherwise, return the k-th happy string in lexicographical order, where `happy_strings[n]` is the list of all happy strings of length n sorted lexicographically.
